accuracy.evidence: Checked against NC 2013 Year 4 Electricity ('recognise that a switch opens and closes a circuit and associate this with whether or not a lamp lights in a simple series circuit') and its non-statutory guidance (making switches), and the IOP 'Supporting Physics Teaching 11-14: Electric circuits' notes: a switch is a pair of conducting contacts; current in a series loop is the same everywhere and starts and stops everywhere at once; the cell provides the push and nothing is stored in the switch. The lab's charge dots all move or all freeze together and never pile up at the gap. Push switches springing open and toggle switches staying put match standard switch types. The door-mat alarm is the common school pressure-pad design (two foil sheets separated by sponge).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented ideas from Shipstone (1984) 'A study of children's understanding of electricity in simple DC circuits' (European Journal of Science Education 6(2)) and Osborne (1983) 'Towards modifying children's ideas about electric current': sequential reasoning that current reaches the bulb before the switch matters (prediction 3, 'after', p5, m4), current piling up at a gap ('pile'), the switch needing to be beside the battery ('batt', m3), switches making or storing electricity ('makes', 'stores', m1), plus the classroom 'open means on' language slip ('openon', prediction 1, p1, m2) and 'either switch is enough' for two in series ('either', p2).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagswitch is about the switch mechanism and its place in a loop: a large cutaway metal strip and contact you drag shut, a paper clip that swings on a pin to bridge a second pin, one switch moved to three slots and opened in each, an AND pair of switches, and three home switches (toggle, spring-back push, pressure mat). flagcdiag teaches symbols, flagcond tests materials, flagseries adds bulbs in series and parallel. Max 6-shingle similarity 2.7% (flag_remd.js); explanation overlap 1.0% (Sound Travels Through Materials).

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner sees each idea before it is stated: all 18 charge dots freeze the instant the strip lifts (not just those past the gap), the buzzer sounds only while the clip touches the second pin, the bulb goes off whichever slot the opened switch is in, the 'Tried 4 of 4 ways' counter shows only one lit setting, and the doorbell stops by itself as its spring opens the contact.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options disproved on screen: 'it lights: open means on' (the open switch leaves the bulb dark), 'it is bendy' for the paper clip (it works because it is metal and closes the gap), and 'the bulb stays on: the current already got there' when the switch is after the bulb (it goes off).

challenge_feedback.evidence: slip() has 10 distinct messages (openon, dim, batt, before, makes, stores, strong, after, pile, either), each naming the slip, e.g. 'Open means there is a gap, so no current can flow. Open is off; closed is on.' and 'Nothing piles up. With a gap, the whole loop stops at the same moment.'

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs FK 1.2 with short sentences (loop, gap, metal bits touch, open means off); adult FK 9.0 within the 9.5 limit; validate_lessons passes for the family audience. 'Conductor', 'series' and 'contacts' stay in the adult panel.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no banned phrases; explanation overlap 1.0% at most). Kid text: loop and gaps, closed, open, open-means-off and placement with home examples. Adult text: objective and key words, how contacts and series current work, named mistakes, what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px Android in light and dark after Show me on every step plus mid-step: the loop, cell, bulb, switch, dashed slots, counters and the three home panels fit and stay readable; after the first screenshots the home bulb and buzzers were moved down so the bulb glow no longer covered the 'Light switch' label. Buttons wrap below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag or tap has a button twin ('Close the switch', 'Swing the clip onto the pin', 'Put it after the bulb', 'Close A' with aria-label 'Close switch A', 'Step on the mat'). The canvas aria-label and narration update after every action, including the doorbell springing back. walk.cjs: desktop and iPhone 13 complete all 5 tasks with Show me, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes, no console errors.
